headline: Building tools in Stockholm's winter
narrative: Quiet week focused on cursor-commands and shipflow, refining the developer tools that make building software easier. The work is surgical—iterating on features that let you stay in flow, never leaving context. Meanwhile, musical taste shifts toward trip hop and neo-psychedelic, exploring French indie pop while dream pop remains the steady foundation.

sections.title: Cursor commands and shipflow
sections.content: Deep work on cursor-commands and shipflow, the point-and-click editing tools powered by Cursor Agent. Contributed a PR to the cursor-commands repo, continuing the vision of making building software easier and more fun. Activity is down slightly (24 commits vs typical 33), but the focus is sharp—surgical moves over sweeping rewrites.

sections.title: Dream pop meets trip hop
sections.content: Core taste holds steady with Beach House and dream pop, but recent exploration leans into trip hop and neo-psychedelic—Massive Attack, Tame Impala, Moby. Discovering French indie pop artists like Videoclub, while 'Intriguing Possibilities' by Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross stays on repeat. The shift feels intentional, matching the focused building energy.

sections.title: Quiet week
sections.content: No posts this week, but recent themes around building with agents, staying in flow, and surgical iterations continue to shape the narrative.

footer: Overcast Stockholm winter, short days ending before three. Building tools in the dim light, where focus sharpens and details matter.
